# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage, and it has three AI use cases:

- A customer service chatbot is deployed on its support portal.
- AI visual inspection is being piloted on its German production line.
- AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. ISO/IEC 42001 is the certification target, with work to start next year. That start date is not yet fixed.

Dana Whitfield stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints apply:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The incumbent frameworks are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. The Case for a Guided Build

A consultant-delivered AIMS can produce documents quickly. However, the people who must run the system have not built it, so they are often unable to explain or defend it. The Guided AI GRC Build reverses that arrangement. The Tamarack Instruments build team produces every artifact, guided by weekly workshops, coaching and structured asynchronous work. At Week 12 the Client's team owns the system, understands why each part exists and can operate it without depending on an outside firm.

The program applies three principles:

- **Slow AI:** AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
- **Informed Intent:** no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human:** every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

The program uses two open frameworks:

- **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) provides the governance, risk and compliance structure.
- **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) provides the governed workflow and human oversight patterns used in Week 9.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored

**Inventory order.** Systems enter the Week 2 inventory in this order:

1. The customer service chatbot enters first because it is deployed and faces customers.
2. The visual inspection pilot enters second because it is tied to the stated Q2 2027 objective.
3. Sales forecasting enters third as a planned system, so that governance precedes its build.

Whether any further AI systems exist is a question to confirm at intake.

**Incumbent integration points.** The program attaches its artifacts to the incumbent frameworks rather than creating parallel structures. Where the specific ISMS or quality management system artifact to attach to is not yet known, it is shown as `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The readiness themes listed for each week indicate preparation only. They do not predict any certification outcome.

| Week | Build focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | Incumbent integration point | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scope covers the three use cases. EU data residency and works council consultation are recorded as charter constraints. | ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS: Unknown. ISO 9001 QMS: Unknown | Context, scope, leadership and roles |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, then visual inspection pilot, then planned sales forecasting. A named owner is assigned per system. | Internal audit function: June 2026 finding (no inventory of AI systems) | Scope of the AIMS |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification of each inventoried system (confirm with external counsel) | ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS: Unknown | Risk criteria and planning |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Chatbot: GDPR and data residency. Visual inspection: quality and production staff impact. Forecasting: scoping only. | ISO 9001 QMS: Unknown | AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Treatment plans prioritise the chatbot and visual inspection | ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS: Unknown | Risk treatment |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | AI policy, acceptable use and data residency provisions (confirm with external counsel) | ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS: Unknown. ISO 9001 QMS: Unknown | AI policy and leadership commitment |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Pilot-to-production gate for visual inspection, including a works council consultation step (confirm with external counsel) | ISO 9001 QMS: Unknown | Operational planning and AI system life cycle |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection starts | Supplier review for each inventoried system. Suppliers are Unknown and will be confirmed at intake. | ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS: Unknown | Third party relationships and documented information |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen, https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) | Two workflows brought under governed operation, with selection confirmed at intake | ISO 9001 QMS: Unknown | Operation and human oversight |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Chatbot output monitoring. Visual inspection evaluation criteria set with the Head of Quality. | ISO 9001 QMS: Unknown | Monitoring, measurement and evaluation |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident route and change control for model updates | ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS: Unknown | Nonconformity, corrective action and change |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Evidence walkthrough with internal auditor roles in a reviewing capacity | Internal audit function: June 2026 finding | Internal audit and management review readiness |

If the program starts by early January 2027, Week 12 falls before the start of Q2 2027.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

At Week 12, Tamarack Instruments will have a minimum viable AIMS consisting of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

The customer service chatbot is a candidate for the first governed workflow. The second workflow is a question to confirm at intake. The visual inspection pilot is a candidate only if it is in production use by Week 9 and works council consultation has been completed. This outcome is a readiness position. It is not a certification, audit or regulatory outcome.

The internal auditors' participation raises a question to confirm at intake: how their build role is kept independent from any later audit of the AIMS.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Week 1 (mobilization), Week 6 (mid-point) and Week 12 (closing). Steering membership is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake. Board-layer material draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Workshop times will be set once participant locations are confirmed at intake.

**Data residency.** The program does not require customer data to leave the EU. Evidence storage locations will be set by the Client.

**Price.** The price is US$60,000. This sits below the US$80,000 budget approved for this fiscal year. Whether program invoicing falls within this fiscal year, and the invoicing schedule, are to be confirmed.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a one-hour intake session before that date to confirm the following:

- Any AI systems beyond the three named use cases.
- Whether the chatbot processes customer data and where (confirm with external counsel).
- Whether the visual inspection pilot touches production staff for works council purposes (confirm with external counsel).
- The second governed workflow.
- Steering membership and participant locations.
- The ISMS and quality management system artifacts that each integration point attaches to.
- Suppliers for each system.
- The ISO/IEC 42001 start date.
- A program start date.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
